niche_preference_profile: This user tends to prefer interfaces that feel visually complete, structured, and intentional. They repeatedly favor strong information hierarchy, visible actions, and populated screens over empty or underfilled layouts. They also often like clear modular grouping, distinct cards or rows, and interfaces that feel polished and finished. A secondary pattern shows preference for open spacing and breathable layouts, but only when the screen still feels organized and informative. Their color and mood preferences are mixed across contexts, alternating between dark high-contrast expressive UIs and light airy restrained ones, so the most stable preference is not a specific theme but clarity, completeness, and deliberate structure.

criteria.description: Prefers screens with clear layered hierarchy through strong headings, section separation, grouped content, and obvious title-to-body-to-action flow.
Prefers interfaces where available actions are clearly exposed through labeled buttons, integrated per-item controls, and obvious next steps rather than hidden or ambiguous controls.
Prefers content organized into clear modular sections, grouped rows, or self-contained cards rather than mixed flows or weakly separated content.
Prefers screens that look filled out, functional, and content-rich, with visible items and complete sections rather than sparse, empty, or placeholder-like states.
Prefers layouts with enough whitespace and spacing to keep sections calm, readable, and clearly separated, as long as the interface still feels structured and complete.
